# Code of Conduct

## 1. Our Commitment

We are committed to providing an open, respectful, inclusive, and constructive environment for everyone participating in this project.

We welcome contributions from individuals regardless of their experience level, background, identity, nationality, or technical expertise.

Our community is built around engineering, learning, collaboration, and mutual respect.

## 2. Expected Behavior

All participants are expected to:

- Communicate respectfully and professionally.
- Be constructive when providing feedback.
- Respect differing opinions and technical approaches.
- Focus discussions on ideas, implementations, and engineering decisions.
- Accept constructive criticism gracefully.
- Provide clear, actionable feedback during code reviews.
- Respect the time and effort of maintainers and contributors.
- Help create an environment where newcomers can participate comfortably.

Technical disagreements are welcome. Personal attacks are not.

## 3. Unacceptable Behavior

The following behaviors are not acceptable:

- Harassment, intimidation, threats, or personal attacks.
- Discriminatory language or conduct.
- Deliberate humiliation or hostile communication.
- Publishing private or personally identifiable information without consent.
- Sexualized language or unwanted sexual attention.
- Trolling, deliberate disruption, or repeated bad-faith arguments.
- Spam, malicious links, or intentionally misleading information.
- Retaliation against individuals who report violations.
- Any conduct that creates an unsafe or hostile community environment.

## 4. Engineering Discussions

Technical discussions should remain professional and evidence-driven.

Participants should:

- Criticize implementations rather than individuals.
- Explain technical disagreements with reasoning.
- Avoid dismissing contributions without constructive feedback.
- Respect architectural decisions made by maintainers.
- Avoid turning code reviews into personal disputes.

Strong technical opinions are encouraged when expressed respectfully.

## 5. Scope

This Code of Conduct applies to all project spaces, including:

- GitHub issues.
- Pull requests.
- Discussions.
- Code reviews.
- Project-related communication channels.
- Official community spaces.
- Other spaces where an individual is representing the project.

## 6. Reporting Violations

If you experience or witness unacceptable behavior, report it privately to:

**Project maintainers:** [Emmanuel A](mailto:aemmanuel685210@gmail.com)

You may also contact the repository owner through GitHub.

Reports should include:

- A description of the incident.
- Relevant links or references.
- Approximate dates and times.
- Any supporting evidence.

Please avoid publicly disclosing sensitive information about the incident.

All reports will be reviewed as confidentially as reasonably possible.

## 7. Enforcement

Project maintainers are responsible for enforcing this Code of Conduct.

Depending on the severity and circumstances, actions may include:

1. A private warning.
2. A request to modify or remove inappropriate content.
3. Temporary restrictions on participation.
4. Removal of comments or contributions.
5. Temporary or permanent exclusion from project spaces.

Maintainers will consider the nature, severity, and context of each incident.

## 8. Responsibilities of Maintainers

Maintainers are expected to:

- Apply these standards consistently.
- Handle reports seriously and professionally.
- Avoid retaliation against reporters.
- Protect confidential information.
- Explain enforcement decisions where appropriate without exposing private details.

## 9. Acknowledgment

Participation in this project implies agreement to follow these community standards.

We reserve the right to update this Code of Conduct as the project evolves.

Our objective is simple: maintain a technically strong, respectful, and productive engineering community.
